label: One record short of the floor: 24 scored prompts, no grade, a named reason instead.
boundary: The other side of the same line as at-threshold-corpus.json. The rubric would happily return a composite of 92 for these 24 records; this module refuses to publish it, and says which floor it fell under.

authoredAgainst.why: Every expected value below was derived by hand from exactly these numbers. If one of them changes, this file is wrong until a person re-derives it — that is the whole reason the numbers are copied here rather than read from the modules.

expectedValuesAreHandAuthored: 24 records carry a category the rubric published (20 high-value, 4 over-provisioned) and 3 carry one it does not, so 27 records were handed in and 24 scored. 24 < 25, so no grade, no composite, and confidence is the named 'none' rather than a number. Classified share = 24 / 27 = 0.888888..., reported to 4 decimals as 0.8889 — above the 0.6 floor, which is why the reason names the record count and nothing else. For the record, the composite this corpus would have scored is (20x100 + 4x55) / 24 = 92; it is not published anywhere in the result. Nothing here was produced by calling the module.
